summary:
NASA Explorer is an interactive web platform and gamified storytelling experience designed to transform discarded lunar and Martian space hardware from forgotten debris into living "Memory Beacons." By utilizing verified NASA historical archives and scientific datasets, we developed an interactive interface where users can explore key landing sites on the Moon and Mars, inspect stranded rovers and landers like Apollo 11 and Opportunity, and read their engineering stories. To keep users engaged, each mission concludes with an interactive quiz challenge where every correct answer rewards the explorer with 250 XP, allowing them to level up as they uncover more space history.

Our project directly addresses the challenge of connecting the public with space exploration heritage and the growing presence of human-made artifacts beyond Earth. Rather than viewing decommissioned spacecraft merely as space junk, NASA Explorer preserves their scientific legacy, educates future generations through simplified data and rewarding progression, and inspires sustainable exploration of our solar system.
details:
What does it do or how does it work? NASA Explorer is an interactive web platform that transforms decommissioned lunar and Martian hardware into living "Memory Beacons." Users navigate through immersive lunar and Martian environments, explore historic landing sites, and inspect rovers like Apollo 11 and Opportunity. After reading the engineering and historical story of each mission, users face interactive quiz challenges. Every correct answer rewards the explorer with 250 XP, driving a gamified progression system that lets users level up as they uncover more space history.

What benefits does it have & what is the intended impact? The platform bridges the gap between complex space archives and the general public. By turning raw technical data into an engaging, story-driven experience, it educates youth and space enthusiasts, shifts public perception of space debris from "trash" to "historical heritage," and inspires responsible, sustainable space exploration.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use? We built the platform using modern web development technologies (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) for the interactive interface, Canva for cinematic visual design and video pitch production, and verified official NASA historical archives and datasets for scientific integrity.

How is it creative & what factors did team Bytee consider? Our project introduces gamified storytelling to space education—combining historical exploration with an XP leveling system. Team Bytee carefully considered user engagement, mobile/web accessibility, the simplification of complex scientific datasets, and a professional leadership and execution structure across our design, search, and development sections.
